ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Duke Kahanamoku

text.paragraph: Subsequent annual wellness visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mr. Kahanamoku returns for his subsequent annual wellness visit; his first was with his previous primary care physician last year. He completed the health risk assessment with the medical assistant. He finished cardiac rehabilitation in the summer and now swims three mornings a week in calm water inside the reef with a friend. He is working full days as sheriff. He has had no swelling, orthopnea or lightheadedness since the spring, and no further illness. He asks what screening he needs. [S]

Next scheduled visit 2026-09-28: six-month review: repeat echocardiogram after more than 90 days of therapy, the defibrillator decision, iron, the delayed titration step, and plans for the year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 25 minutes, with his consent and, at his wish, with members of his ʻohana present. He named a member of his ʻohana as his health care agent, and the Hawaiʻi advance health care directive was completed and copied into the chart. He wants full treatment, including resuscitation, for illness he can recover from. If his heart failure advanced so that he could no longer leave his bed, he would want comfort and time at home over repeated hospital stays. If a defibrillator is ever offered, he wants to talk about it with his ʻohana first. He asked that his own Hawaiian practices at the end of life be respected as he and his ʻohana choose; they were not described and nothing further was asked. [S]
